name.description: EOSIO account / scope identifier. Encoded into a uint64 by mapping each character to a 5-bit symbol; positions 0-11 use the full alphabet, the 13th character (if present) only has 4 bits available.
constraints: 1 to 13 characters, lowercase
Allowed characters: a-z, 1-5, and '.'
If 13 characters, the 13th must be one of [.1-5a-j] (4-bit slot)
No uppercase letters, digits 0/6-9, or special characters other than '.'
Empty string is not a valid name

account_name.description: Alias for `name` used to identify a chain account. Same encoding and validation rules as `name`.
constraints: Must reference an account that exists on the active chain
1 to 13 characters, charset [.1-5a-z], 13th char restricted to [.1-5a-j]

permission_name.description: Alias for `name` identifying a permission level on an account (e.g. 'owner', 'active', or a custom permission).
constraints: Same charset/length rules as `name`
Common values: 'owner', 'active'; contracts may declare custom permissions

asset.description: Quantity + symbol pair. String form is '<amount> <symbol_code>' where the amount has exactly the symbol's precision number of fractional digits.
constraints: Format: '<amount> <symbol_code>' with a single space separator
Amount is a signed decimal; |amount * 10^precision| must fit in int64 (≤ 2^62 - 1)
Number of fractional digits must equal the symbol's precision (0-18)
Symbol code is 1-7 uppercase letters (A-Z) only
Examples must match the precision used at issuance — '1 UOS' is invalid for the 4-decimal core symbol; use '1.0000 UOS'

extended_asset.description: An `asset` qualified by the issuing contract account. JSON form is { quantity: asset, contract: account_name }.
constraints: Object with keys `quantity` (asset) and `contract` (account_name)
Both fields are required and validated by their underlying type rules
Used when the same symbol can be issued by multiple contracts and the contract must be disambiguated

symbol.description: Currency symbol with explicit precision. String form is '<precision>,<code>'.
constraints: Format: '<precision>,<symbol_code>'
Precision is an integer 0-18 (max_precision in chain/symbol.hpp)
Symbol code is 1-7 uppercase letters (A-Z)

symbol_code.description: The currency code portion of a symbol, without precision.
constraints: 1-7 uppercase letters (A-Z)
No digits, lowercase, or punctuation

extended_symbol.description: A `symbol` qualified by the issuing contract account. JSON form is { sym: symbol, contract: account_name }.
constraints: Object with keys `sym` (symbol) and `contract` (account_name)
Both fields are required and validated by their underlying type rules
ISO 8601 datetime in UTC with no timezone suffix (no trailing 'Z' or offset)
Optional fractional seconds with up to 6 digits (microseconds)
Range is bounded by int64 microseconds since the Unix epoch
ISO 8601 datetime in UTC with no fractional seconds and no timezone suffix
Backed by uint32 seconds since the Unix epoch (year 2106 max)

block_timestamp_type.description: Half-second-aligned timestamp used for block production. Encoded as 500 ms ticks since the EOSIO epoch (2000-01-01T00:00:00.000).
constraints: ISO 8601 datetime aligned to a 500 ms boundary (fractional seconds end in .000 or .500)
EOSIO epoch is 2000-01-01T00:00:00 — values before this are invalid
Stored as uint32 slot count, so the practical max is ~year 2068

public_key.description: Public key in base58 form. Two encodings exist: the legacy 'EOS'-prefixed K1 key (no underscore separator) and the modern 'PUB_<curve>_<base58>' form.
constraints: Legacy form: 'EOS' followed by base58 data (≈50 chars); no underscore
Modern form: 'PUB_K1_' (secp256k1), 'PUB_R1_' (secp256r1/NIST P-256), or 'PUB_WA_' (WebAuthn) followed by base58 data
Base58 alphabet is Bitcoin's: 1-9, A-Z (no I O), a-z (no l)
The trailing checksum is verified by ultra-signer-lib; do not validate it client-side

signature.description: Signature in base58 form, always prefixed with 'SIG_<curve>_'. Curve must match the key that produced it.
constraints: 'SIG_K1_' (secp256k1), 'SIG_R1_' (secp256r1), or 'SIG_WA_' (WebAuthn)
Base58 payload uses Bitcoin's alphabet (no 0, O, I, l)
The toolkit never asks the LLM to construct signatures — wallets sign; this type appears in catalog field hints only

checksum256.description: SHA-256 hash rendered as a hex string.
constraints: Exactly 64 lowercase hex characters
No '0x' prefix

bytes.description: Arbitrary binary blob rendered as a hex string.
constraints: Hex-encoded, even number of characters (each byte = 2 hex chars)
No '0x' prefix and no whitespace separators
Empty string is permitted and represents zero bytes
